_comment: PRD-261 B-03e1: the shared review corpus. Core's review stage (orchestrator/services/themes/review_stage.py, run by orchestrator/tests/test_prd261_review_corpus.py) and the kit's automatos-theme check (which vendors this file from core byte for byte) each review every case and must give the level in expected for each check named in checks. A case is the hello package (orchestrator/tests/fixtures/themes/hello, which the kit vendors from the same commit) changed as orchestrator/tests/fixtures/themes/build.py changes it: manifestSet sets top-level theme.json fields over hello's, manifestUnset removes them, and the result is written as JSON with two-space indent and a final newline; replace sets a file's text (a path hello lacks adds the file) or, with null, drops it. Files are packed in path order. Every case is a package the reader accepts, so sizes, cssScope and looks are the reader's checks recorded as passed (a refused package never reaches the review; cases.json's packages section holds the refusals). The SDK names are the host's own list, services/themes/data/sdk-surface.json at the same commit; a case whose host is {"sdkSurface": "missing"} is reviewed as on a host that has no readable SDK name list. Anywhere in a case, {"$corePageSha": path} stands for that core page file's sha256 as services/themes/data/core-pages.json at the same commit gives it, so no page edit changes this file. The LLM stage is not part of the corpus (core runs it with a fake answering risk 0; it is the server's own check), and neither is contrast (its mobile cases are in test_prd261_review_stage.py). The file is held to its canonical form, json.dumps with indent 2 and a final newline, so its sha256 changes only when a case does.
